context:
Goal: batches merge faster.
Problem (rule): draft runs of the tests a lane touches take the macOS runners the batch needs; skipping them narrows your Nov 8 ruling.
Based on (ruling): your Nov 8, 06:08 CST pick (step windows-tests-for-touched-files): a draft-only CI job runs just the test files a lane touches, on Windows and on macOS where a macOS job exists.
Based on (measured): batch 103's run 43234925158 waited 26.4 min for macOS while 50 draft runs ran, 13:30-14:40 UTC.
Departs from: your Nov 8 pick, where drafts always run macOS — drafts skip it while a batch runs, or always.
home: step ci-macos-queue (batches stop waiting for macOS)

lastAnswer.note: Owner 14:19 CST in retrospective chat, with his pick e on the MacBook item (R58, plan 0a36899): a draft's macOS job skips while a batch run is in progress.

options.gain: The batch run ends sooner (about 40 min, not 55; estimate).
options.how: A draft run skips macOS while a batch's CI is running.
options.label: Skip while a batch runs (Recommended)
options.lose: A macOS-only failure in a draft pushed then shows at the next batch.

options.label: Drafts never run macOS
options.lose: Every macOS-only failure first shows in a batch, so more drops.

options.label: Keep as is
options.lose: Batches keep waiting up to 26 min.

reply: Closed 14:22 CST: step ci-batch-mac-runner, lane started.
short: Drafts skip macOS during a batch
title: Draft runs skip macOS while a batch's CI runs
why: It narrows your Nov 8 ruling that every draft runs its touched tests on Windows and macOS.
